author: claude

patch.value: The preflight asks npm's OIDC exchange endpoint for a credential before the version bump and fails the run when npm refuses. The verifier is registered in release:check and was confirmed to pass before being wired in.
A release run bumped and committed a new version every night while publishing was impossible, and the changelog-date verifier no gate ever invoked

Two defects in the same release path. Publication is the only step that can fail for a reason outside this repository and it runs last, so ten days of a dead npm credential still advanced main every night and published nothing. Separately, scripts/verify-release-changelog-date.sh proved the untagged-release heading comes from the calendar version rather than the clock, but no package script or workflow ever invoked it, which makes it documentation rather than a gate.

The release run fails before the version bump when npm will not accept the workflow's OIDC identity; release:check invokes verify-release-changelog-date so a generator regression cannot merge unrun; the package's own six release-transaction tests are preserved alongside the seven OIDC guards

message: Record the release-ordering defect and the unwired changelog-date verifier

value.author: claude
value.text: Verified by mutation rather than inspection. Twenty reverts were applied to the workflow one at a time and the guard suite re-run against each, and all twenty fail, including reintroducing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, deleting the preflight, marking it continue-on-error, loosening the npm pin, dropping the setup-node _authToken strip, a --global npm downgrade, credential aliases _auth username and keyfile, NPM_CONFIG__AUTH, a comment-only npm install, three job-permission override spellings, a fixed /tmp credential path, mktemp without the cleanup trap, and a bracket-form secret reference.

value.author: claude
value.text: Root cause was established by asking the registry, not by reading CI. A throwaway workflow minted a GitHub OIDC id-token of 1982 bytes and offered it to npm's exchange endpoint, which answered HTTP 404 with 'OIDC token exchange error - package not found'. That is npm reporting no trusted publisher binding rather than a missing package. Publishing stays blocked until a trusted publisher is configured on npmjs.com, which is outside this repository.

value.author: claude
value.text: The seven canonical OIDC guards were merged into this package's existing suite rather than replacing it. Its six release-transaction tests are unique to pm-changelog and are preserved, so thirteen tests now run. The changelog-date verifier was executed and confirmed passing before being registered in release:check, rather than wired in and assumed green.

value.author: claude
value.text: Round-4 review found a defect that would have blocked every correct release, which is worse than the outage the preflight exists to prevent. The exchange URL was built from the raw package.json name, so a scoped name such as @unbrained/pm-web addressed a different path entirely instead of %40unbrained%2Fpm-web; and only HTTP 200 was accepted while npm answers 201 on a successful exchange. Both are fixed: the name is encoded with encodeURIComponent, and any 2xx is accepted. Two bypasses were also closed: the preflight's if: could be changed to false, leaving the step present, correctly ordered and never executed while the bump commit and publish steps still ran, so the exact release condition is now pinned and must match the one the mutating steps use; and a second trap EXIT silently replaces the first, so exactly one trap is now permitted. Four more reverts verified, twenty-four in total.
